info.title: m-gated management API
info.description:
The management API of m-gated. It covers a person's own data and virtual keys under `/api/`, and admin work under `/api/admin/`. Only admins can call routes under `/api/admin/`. The inference routes (such as `/v1/messages`) and the browser sign-in routes under `/auth/` are not in this document.

## Credentials

Send one of these credentials:

- A sign-in token: the SSO token in `sso` mode, or the session token in `password` mode. Send it in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or in the session cookie.
- A management token. It starts with `mgt_`. An admin issues it on the dashboard or with `POST /api/admin/management-tokens`. Send it only in `Authorization: Bearer mgt_...`. A management token in a cookie or in `x-api-key` gets `401 invalid_credentials`. A token acts as the admin who issued it.

A `read` management token can call only GET routes. A `write` token can call every route that accepts tokens. In each operation, `x-token-scope` names the scope that the operation needs. It is null when the route does not accept management tokens. Such a call gets `403 management_token_not_allowed`.

Virtual keys (`mgw_...`) are for inference only. The management API rejects them.

`x-role` names the role that may call an operation: `user` (every person on the access list) or `admin`. An operation with `x-auth-mode: password` exists only when the gateway runs in `password` mode.

## CSRF

A write (any method other than GET) with the credential in a cookie also needs two headers: `Origin` with the gateway's public origin, and `X-CSRF-Token` with a token from `GET /api/csrf`. A browser never adds an `Authorization` header by itself, so a write with an `Authorization` header needs no CSRF token.

## Commands

Every write except `POST /api/me/password` needs the `X-Gateway-Command-ID` header with a UUID that the client makes. In each operation, `x-command-id` says whether it needs the header. The gateway keeps the result of each command. When the same caller sends a command again with the same ID and the same input, the gateway does not run it again. It returns the first result, and the response has the header `x-gateway-command-replayed: true`. The same ID with a different input gets `409 command_conflict`. A command that returns a secret (a new virtual key or management token) cannot give the secret again. Its repeat gets `409 key_secret_unavailable` or `409 management_token_secret_unavailable`.

Many writes need `expected_version`, the version that the client read. When the version changed, the write gets `409 version_conflict`, and `error.details.current_version` holds the current version. Versions, counts and amounts are decimal strings.

## Errors

Every error has the same body:

```json
{"error": {"code": "access_denied", "message": "...", "request_id": "...", "details": {}}}
```

`code` is stable and machine-readable. The `x-gateway-error-code` header has the same value. `message` is for people and can change. `details` is an object. It is empty unless the code says otherwise. Each error response of an operation lists its codes in `x-error-codes`. The top-level `x-common-errors` lists the codes that any route can return, for example when the gateway is overloaded, a dependency is down, or the path or method is unknown. A `503` response has `Retry-After: 1`.

These codes mean the same on every route:

- `invalid_request` (400): The body, a path parameter, the query or a header is not valid. A missing or malformed `X-Gateway-Command-ID` also gets this code.
- `invalid_filter` (400): A query parameter is unknown, repeated or not valid.
- `invalid_cursor` (400): The cursor is not valid, has expired, or does not match the other query parameters.
- `invalid_credentials` (401): The credential is missing, unknown, expired or revoked.
- `access_denied` (403): The caller is not on the access list, is suspended, or does not have the admin role that this route needs.
- `management_token_not_allowed` (403): A management token cannot call this route, or a `read` token tried to write.
- `origin_denied` (403): A write with a cookie credential did not send exactly one `Origin` header with the gateway's public origin.
- `csrf_invalid` (403): A write with a cookie credential did not send exactly one valid `X-CSRF-Token` header.
- `resource_not_found` (404): The resource does not exist, or the caller cannot see it.
- `request_body_timeout` (408): The client did not send the whole body within 5 seconds.
- `body_too_large` (413): The body is larger than the limit for management requests (64 KiB by default).
- `unsupported_media_type` (415): The body is not identity-encoded, or `Content-Type` is not `application/json`.
- `command_conflict` (409): The command ID was already used with a different input.
- `version_conflict` (409): `expected_version` is not the current version. `details.current_version` holds the current version.

The codes in `x-common-errors` mean:

- `auth_source_forbidden` (403): The credential came from a source that this route does not accept, for example a virtual key, or an `Authorization` header where only the session cookie is accepted.
- `owner_inactive` (403): The credential is a virtual key whose owner is not active.
- `route_not_found` (404): No route has this path.
- `method_not_allowed` (405): The path does not allow this method. The `Allow` header lists the allowed methods.
- `concurrency_limited` (429): The gateway has no free request slot. Retry later.
- `header_limit` (431): The request headers are too many or too large.
- `invariant_violation` (500): The gateway found an internal state that should not happen.
- `not_ready` (503): The gateway or one of its dependencies is not ready.
- `draining` (503): The gateway is shutting down.
- `auth_dependency_unavailable` (503): The gateway could not check the credential now.
- `db_unavailable` (503): The database is not available, or the request took too long.
- `command_busy` (503): The command could not get its locks in time. Retry with the same command ID.
